review.purpose: Separate decoded image dimensions/format from byte identity and metadata.
review.finding: Three generated files all decode to 160 by120 pixels, with PNG/JPEG formats, but have three distinct byte SHA-256 identities. The second story reuses image_info on returned BLOBs to verify dimensions and formats; source size alone is not output storage size.

review.purpose: Retain missing GPS as a distinct state and inspect metadata disagreements among perceptually similar files.
review.finding: Only the deliberately tagged JPEG has a GPS result. The zero-pHash-distance JPEG pair has different GPS presence and different byte hashes. Raising the review threshold selects additional pairs without changing any metadata; missing GPS is not interpreted as a zero coordinate.

review.purpose: Build perceptual review candidates without equating them to byte-identical files.
review.finding: The generated JPEG pair has zero pHash distance despite distinct file bytes; each PNG/JPEG pair differs by12bits. The inclusive8-bit rule selects one of three pairs;16bits selects all three. This related fixture cannot estimate library-scale accuracy.

review.purpose: Compare a different fingerprint method on the same fixed population.
review.finding: All three unique pairs have zero dHash distance while byte identities remain distinct and pHash/aHash differ on PNG/JPEG pairs. A zero method-specific distance does not prove identical bytes, metadata or equal calibration across algorithms.

review.purpose: Expose algorithm-specific sensitivity using the same related files.
review.finding: aHash differs by one bit for each PNG/JPEG pair and by zero for the JPEG pair; dHash is zero throughout and pHash reaches12. The chart states its observed0–12scale and the possible0–64range. Equal numeric thresholds are not established as equivalent between algorithms.

review.purpose: Measure Hamming distance across same-width fingerprints and apply a transparent inclusive review rule.
review.finding: Three unique pairs are accounted for. The8→16-bit experiment changes candidates1→3 while all source facts and distances remain fixed. Eight invariants check bounds, self-distance, symmetry, hash type and population accounting; selection does not authorize deletion.

review.purpose: Inspect the full EXIF map before and after re-encoding rather than substituting a preview for metadata evidence.
review.finding: The source has four deliberately injected GPS-related EXIF entries. All three returned encodings expose empty EXIF maps and absent GPS through this reader. An observed empty map is not a universal metadata-sanitization or privacy guarantee.

review.purpose: Measure the zero-configuration JPEG thumbnail as a separate artifact contract.
review.finding: The default128-pixel JPEG box returns128 by96 pixels and3069bytes, versus160 by120 and4750bytes in the source. EXIF/GPS are absent. This row remains unchanged when only the explicit PNG box changes; the source is retained.

review.purpose: Test the explicit PNG bounding box, measured storage and released upscale behavior.
review.finding: At80pixels the released worker returns80 by60pixels and6059bytes; at240 it returns240 by180 and33579bytes. The experiment changes only that rendition, keeps source/default/BMP fixed, and demonstrates the old release upscaling. Current public source has a no-upscale guard and would retain160 by120; current runtime is not claimed tested.

review.purpose: Separate full-size container conversion from thumbnail dimensions and encoded storage size.
review.finding: BMP conversion keeps160 by120pixels but grows to57654bytes and loses the observed EXIF/GPS results. Dimensions do not prove pixel identity or image quality. The BMP row is unchanged by the PNG-box experiment, and all11 artifact checks pass.
